children: rose 1.2% in Thursday's trading as Wells Fargo upgraded the utility to Overweight from Equal Weight with a $118 price target, raised from $108, viewing the stock as a "defensive diversification away from the broader AI trade."
Wells Fargo analyst Shar Pourreza said he has flagged Consolidated Edison
as a "defensive diversification away from the broader AI trade with an electrification/reliability growth story which can prove out well over the next several weeks heading into midterms."

provides "some balance and normalcy as we head into the peak anti-utility midterm finale in November," and "with the macro backdrop more uncertain into November, we see the case for increased investor interest due to its defensive positioning among our coverage," according to Pourreza.
Broader affordability matters are a key debate but not necessarily an earnings risk for Con Ed

, the analyst said, viewing the issue as "longer dated, with no active cases and limited risk to the EPS outlook" and continuing to view affordability as "more of a bill-optics issue than a material threat to authorized returns."
Prediction markets continue to imply Gov. Hochul's re-election, but importantly, Con Ed

has settled all rate cases, with CECONY E&G under multi-year plans through 2028, "leaving other New York utilities as the first test cases under Chapter 58's budget-constraint framework," Pourreza wrote.

title: Consolidated Edison upgraded at Wells Fargo as buffer against AI trade rotation
